what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to approve a surrounding community agreement with the casino developer, after extended questions on traffic and mitigation funds.
The board accepted the energy reduction plan from the Green Communities task force, a step toward Green Communities status.
Under the agreement as described, the developer would make a nominal annual payment to Lunenburg plus reimbursement of public safety response costs.
The board reviewed borrowing scenarios for the middle/high school project; a 30-year term costs the average home less per year than 20 years but adds much more interest.
First-quarter figures showed revenues and new growth ahead of budget, while legal spending ran high and a transfer may be needed.

why_it_matters: The casino agreement sets what Lunenburg receives for policing and other response costs, which are paid from the town budget, mostly taxes.
The school borrowing term decides the yearly tax-bill impact against total interest paid over the life of the loan, so a longer term lowers each year's bill but raises the overall cost.
Legal costs and veterans benefits running over budget could require transfers that draw on other town funds.
watch_next: The Dunkin Donuts license request returns on next Tuesday's agenda.
The November 5th meeting is to take up town manager and board goals and Green Communities task force membership and quorum.
